items.label: Ni-Mo-Ta diffusion triples
items.purity: nickel (99.97 pct), pure molybdenum bar (99.97 pct), and pure tantalum bar (99.95 pct)
items.quote: bar (99.97 pct), and pure tantalum bar (99.95 pct), provided by GE Company (Schenectady, NY). At first, the Mo-Ta binary couple was prepared by diffusion welding in a GLEEBLE-1500-type Thermal Simulator. The welding was conducted in vacuum (better than 3 3 1023 Pa) at 1473 to 1573 K under a certain force for 20 to 30 minutes. The binary couples and Ni pieces were then polished and welded together, also in the GLEEBLE-1500-type Thermal Simulator, to form well-contacted Ni-Mo-Ta diffusion triples.
items.starting_materials: electrolytic nickel (99.97 pct), pure molybdenum bar (99.97 pct), and pure tantalum bar (99.95 pct), provided by GE Company (Schenectady, NY)

items.atmosphere_or_container: evacuated silica capsules with a vacuum (3 3 1023 Pa)
items.quote: The triples were sealed in evacuated silica capsules with a vacuum (3 3 1023 Pa) and heated in a GK2B-type diffusion furnace at 1473 K for 200 hours, at 1373 K for 500 hours, and at 1173 K for 1000 hours. The temperature was controlled within 65 K. After annealing, the triples were air quenched.
